title: Position becomes a rotation.
subtitle: Turn three coordinate pairs at different frequencies and inspect how position changes their phase.

steps.title: Split into pairs
steps.body: A six-dimensional vector is split into three two-dimensional pairs. Each ring shows one pair, initially (1, 0). The rings are stacked only to separate them visually; depth is the pair index, not an extra embedding coordinate.

steps.title: Move through the sequence
steps.body: At position m, pair i rotates by m × 10000^(−2i/6) radians. The first pair turns rapidly; later pairs change more slowly. Every pair keeps its length.

steps.title: Compare relative positions
steps.body: Applying these rotations to queries and keys makes their inner product depend on their relative position. This scene shows the rotations only; it does not compute attention, train embeddings, or model long-context extensions.

notes.caption: Interactive 3D on synthetic inputs. No benchmark results are implied.
notes.methods: At position m, pair i rotates by m × 10000^(−2i/6) radians. The first pair turns rapidly; later pairs change more slowly. Every pair keeps its length.
notes.assumptions: Applying these rotations to queries and keys makes their inner product depend on their relative position. This scene shows the rotations only; it does not compute attention, train embeddings, or model long-context extensions.

title: Append once. Read the growing past.
subtitle: Step through decoding and see keys and values accumulate in separate banks for each layer.

steps.title: Keep keys and values
steps.body: Each layer retains the keys and values of earlier tokens. The violet bank stores keys; the green bank stores values. Columns are token positions and rows are three illustrative layers.

steps.title: Append the new token
steps.body: Changing the token count highlights the newest column in amber. Earlier columns stay in place. Thin paths from the current query show that attention still reads every cached key and uses the corresponding values.

steps.title: Account for growing memory
steps.body: Each tile stands for a whole per-token tensor, not one scalar. Head and feature dimensions are collapsed. This is a conceptual dynamic cache with three layers, not a measured memory layout or latency benchmark.

notes.assumptions: Each tile stands for a whole per-token tensor, not one scalar. Head and feature dimensions are collapsed. This is a conceptual dynamic cache with three layers, not a measured memory layout or latency benchmark.
